zh.title: 1839：摄影第一次变成可复制的图像
zh.summary: 达盖尔法公布后，图像第一次能稳定地留在金属板上，也被复制、传播和收藏。它改变了“看见”的权力。

zh.title: 1895：电影成为公共娱乐
zh.summary: 卢米埃尔兄弟把放映变成买票、坐下、一起看。电影从技术演示变成了一种公共时间。

zh.title: 动画史：从赛璐珞到 3D
zh.summary: 从纸、赛璐珞到多边形，工具换了几轮，动画师每天面对的仍是同一个问题：怎么让静止的东西看起来想动。

zh.title: 媒介素养：一条视频的五个问题
zh.summary: 不要先问“真的假的”，先问：谁做的、剪掉了什么、放在什么语境、为什么现在推给我。

zh.title: 版权：先查五件事，再发布
zh.summary: 画面、音乐、字体、肖像、场地，五项分别授权。CC 与商用授权不是一回事。

zh.title: 从银版到手机：摄影的五次转身
zh.summary: 1839 年要坐着不动几十秒，1888 年柯达把相机交给普通人，1975 年传感器把光变成文件，2007 年手机让拍照变成默认动作。

zh.title: 脸为什么越来越近：从影院到手机
zh.summary: 景别不是导演突然爱拍特写，是屏幕变了。影院银幕能装下一张脸，电视只给你一个客厅，手机只给你拇指宽。观众离画面越近，脸就得越大。

zh.title: 暗箱：图像先学会倒过来
zh.summary: 暗箱早就知道光会成像，真正的新东西是它把“看见”变成可以复制的证据。

zh.title: 平台规则：什么会被限流
zh.summary: 平台规则不是玄学；重复搬运、夸大承诺、诱导互动和敏感画面，是最常见的限流点。

zh.title: 无障碍字幕：让听不见的人也跟上
zh.summary: 无障碍字幕要让听不见的人知道谁在说、发生了什么、语气是什么，不只写台词。

zh.title: 迈布里奇：马跑起来的那一秒
zh.summary: 迈布里奇用一排相机拆开马的运动，第一次让人看见肉眼来不及看的瞬间。

zh.title: 爱迪生 Kinetoscope：一个人看的电影
zh.summary: 活动电影放映机把影像装进盒子，一次只给一个人看；电影还没成为公共空间。

zh.title: 卢米埃尔：火车进站吓到观众
zh.summary: 卢米埃尔把火车进站投在墙上，观众第一次被“假的东西”吓到。

zh.title: 蒙太奇：镜头开始有因果
zh.summary: 蒙太奇把两个不相干的镜头剪在一起，观众开始自己造因果。

zh.title: 有声片：观众第一次听见对白
zh.summary: 有声片让电影从“看动作”变成“听人说话”，也逼着摄影棚改变拍法。

zh.title: 特艺彩色：颜色变成卖点
zh.summary: 特艺彩色不是自然色，它把颜色变成奇观，让观众愿意为“更红”买票。

zh.title: 16mm：电影从影院走到教室
zh.summary: 16mm 让摄影机变轻、变便宜，电影从影院走进教室、工厂和田野。

zh.title: 录像带：电视可以重播
zh.summary: 录像带让电视不再只能直播，节目可以录、可以剪、可以重播。

zh.title: 数字影院：胶片退场
zh.summary: 数字影院把胶片从放映环节拿掉，影院开始用硬盘和服务器放映。

zh.title: 单反拍视频：电影感下沉
zh.summary: 单反拍视频把大传感器和可换镜头交给普通人，电影感开始下沉。

zh.title: 手机影像：人人都有摄影机
zh.summary: 手机影像把摄影机变成随身物，拍摄从事件变成日常。

zh.title: 流媒体：观看从频道变成列表
zh.summary: 流媒体把观看从频道时间表变成一张列表，片长和开头都被重新设计。

zh.title: 特效史：从玻璃绘景到 CG
zh.summary: 特效史从玻璃绘景、微缩模型走到 CG，工具变了，问题还是“怎么让假的东西可信”。

zh.title: AI 影像前史：从滤镜到生成
zh.summary: AI 影像不是从生成视频开始；滤镜、修复、抠像、换脸，每一步都在训练“自动修改画面”。

zh.title: 来源核查：这条视频最初是谁发的
zh.summary: 来源核查先找最初发布者，再找原始文件；转发十万次，也不等于真实。

zh.title: 剪辑操控：删掉哪一句改变了意思
zh.summary: 剪辑操控常常只删一句话：删掉前提，结论就变了。

zh.title: 算法推荐：为什么你总看到同一种
zh.summary: 算法推荐按停留和互动放大相似内容；你越停，它越认定你喜欢。

zh.title: 标题党：标题承诺了什么，正文给了什么
zh.summary: 标题党先承诺一个强结果，正文只给一个弱例子；判断方法是把标题和正文各写一句。

zh.title: 深伪识别：看脸之外看什么
zh.summary: 深伪识别别只看脸；看牙齿、耳朵、眨眼、背景文字和光影方向。

zh.title: 数据视频：图表有没有骗人
zh.summary: 数据视频先看坐标轴从哪开始、总数是多少、比较的是不是同一群人。

zh.title: 赞助披露：广告要让人看见
zh.summary: 赞助披露要在观众看到推荐之前出现，不要藏在简介最后一行。

zh.title: 新闻视频：现场、二手信源与核实
zh.summary: 新闻视频先分现场、二手信源和核实；没有核实的“现场”只是素材。

zh.title: 肖像、场地与未成年人授权：一张 Release 要写什么
zh.summary: 拍摄同意不等于商用同意。肖像权、场地物权、未成年人监护人同意、AI 换脸/合成，是四份不同的授权；一张“同意拍摄”纸条救不了广告投放。

zh.title: 隐私与打码：什么时候必须处理
zh.summary: 打码不是礼貌，是义务：住址、车牌、病历、未成年人，能识别就要处理。

zh.title: 合同范围：把“再改一版”写进价格之前
zh.summary: 影视合同最常见的争议不是付款，是范围。交付物、修改轮次、素材版权、验收标准、终止条件没写清，最后都会变成免费加班。

zh.title: 音乐授权：同步权、表演权与平台曲库
zh.summary: “买了这首歌”不等于“能商用”。影视项目至少要区分同步权（把歌录进片子）、表演权（公开播放）、机械复制权（复制音频）和录音制作者权。

zh.title: 场地许可：纸要写什么
zh.summary: 场地许可写清拍摄时间、区域、干扰、损坏责任和成片使用权。

zh.title: AI 内容标识：显式、隐式与平台责任
zh.summary: AI 生成内容不是“标注一下”就合规。中国大陆的标识规则区分显式标识与隐式标识，平台、工具提供者、发布者各有义务；广告与新闻场景更严。

zh.title: 纪录片伦理：拍脆弱的人
zh.summary: 拍脆弱的人先问三件事：他知不知道后果、能不能退出、片子会不会伤害他。

zh.title: 素材安全：客户隐私与泄露
zh.summary: 素材安全包括硬盘、云盘、聊天记录和转发权限；客户隐私不是只有正片。

zh.title: 器材与制作保险：保什么、不保什么
zh.summary: 设备险不是“坏了就赔”。要区分财产一切险、机器损坏险、公众责任险、货运险；免赔额、折旧、除外责任和理赔材料决定你能不能拿到钱。

zh.title: 跨境制作发票与税务：合同、发票、代扣代缴
zh.summary: 跨境项目最容易在“发票”上卡住：客户要的形式发票不是税务发票；服务发生地、收款主体、常设机构、代扣代缴决定税负。先让财税确认路径，再报价。

zh.title: 影像史：1839、1895、摄影史
zh.summary: 影像史不是年份表；1839、1895 和摄影史放在一起，才看得出“记录”如何变成“叙事”。

zh.title: 版权链：版权、合同、音乐
zh.summary: 版权不是一句“已授权”；版权、合同和音乐许可要能对上使用场景、期限和地域。

zh.title: 媒介素养：素养、来源、算法
zh.summary: 媒介素养不是“别信网上的”；来源、算法和情绪触发要拆成可检查的步骤。

zh.title: AI 合规：标识、深伪、数据
zh.summary: AI 合规不是加一行免责声明；标识、深伪和数据来源要一起过。

zh.title: 平台史：从频道到推荐流
zh.summary: 平台不是中立容器；从频道到推荐流，入口、注意力和时长变了，影像语法也跟着变。

zh.title: 档案伦理：修复、删改与署名
zh.summary: 档案不是中性素材；修复、删改和署名都在改写历史，必须留下原件、范围和授权记录。

en.title: 1839: Photography Becomes a Reproducible Image
en.summary: After the Daguerreotype was made public, images could be fixed on metal, copied, circulated, and collected. It changed who could claim to show the world.

en.title: 1895: Cinema Becomes Public Entertainment
en.summary: The Lumières turned projection into a ticket, a seat, and a shared audience. Cinema moved from technical demo to public time.

en.title: Animation History: From Cels to 3D
en.summary: Paper, cels, polygons: the tools changed. Animators still face the same daily problem: how to make a still thing look like it wants to move.

en.title: Media Literacy: Five Questions for Any Video
en.summary: Do not start with “is it real.” Start with: who made it, what was cut, what context, and why it reached me now.

en.title: Rights: Check Five Things Before Publishing
en.summary: Footage, music, fonts, likeness, and location are five separate permissions. CC is not a commercial license.

en.title: From Daguerreotype to Phone: Five Turns in Photography
en.summary: In 1839 you sat still for dozens of seconds. In 1888 Kodak handed the camera to ordinary people. In 1975 a sensor turned light into a file. In 2007 the phone made photographing the default.

en.title: Why Faces Got Closer: Cinema to Phone
en.summary: Faces did not get closer because directors fell in love with close-ups. The screen changed. Cinema could hold a face; TV gave it a living room; the phone gives it a thumb.

en.title: Camera Obscura: The Image Learned to Stand Upside Down
en.summary: The camera obscura already knew light could form an image; what changed was turning sight into reproducible evidence.

en.title: Platform Rules: What Gets Throttled
en.summary: Platform limits are not magic: reposts, exaggerated promises, engagement bait, and sensitive images get throttled.

en.title: Accessible Captions: Let People Who Cannot Hear Follow
en.summary: Accessible captions tell Deaf viewers who speaks, what happens, and how it sounds, not just the words.

en.title: Muybridge: The Second a Horse Ran
en.summary: Muybridge lined up cameras to split a horse's gait and showed a moment the eye could not catch.

en.title: Edison's Kinetoscope: Cinema for One
en.summary: The Kinetoscope put moving images in a box for one viewer; cinema had not become a public space yet.

en.title: Lumière: The Train That Made People Flinch
en.summary: The Lumière brothers projected a train arriving, and the audience flinched at something not there.

en.title: Montage: Shots Learned to Mean
en.summary: Montage cut unrelated shots together and let the audience build the cause.

en.title: Sound Era: The Voice Arrived
en.summary: Sound turned cinema from watching action to hearing people, and forced studios to change how they shot.

en.title: Technicolor: Color Became a Selling Point
en.summary: Technicolor was not natural color; it made color a spectacle worth buying a ticket for.

en.title: 16mm: Cinema Left the Theater
en.summary: 16mm made cameras light and cheap, taking cinema into classrooms, factories, and fields.

en.title: Video Tape: Television Could Replay
en.summary: Video tape freed television from live-only and made recording, editing, and replay possible.

en.title: Digital Cinema: Film Left the Projector
en.summary: Digital cinema removed film from projection; theaters began running from drives and servers.

en.title: DSLR Video: The Cinematic Look Went Downmarket
en.summary: DSLR video put big sensors and interchangeable lenses in ordinary hands; the cinematic look went downmarket.

en.title: Smartphone Video: Everyone Has a Camera
en.summary: Smartphone video made the camera wearable; shooting moved from event to everyday.

en.title: Streaming: Watching Became a List
en.summary: Streaming turned viewing from a schedule into a list, and redesigned length and openings.

en.title: VFX History: From Glass Paintings to CG
en.summary: VFX moved from glass paintings and miniatures to CG; tools changed, the problem stayed: make the fake believable.

en.title: AI Video Prehistory: From Filters to Generation
en.summary: AI video did not start with generation; filters, restoration, matting, and face swap each trained automatic image changes.

en.title: Source Check: Who Posted It First?
en.summary: Find the first poster and the original file; a hundred thousand reposts prove nothing.

en.title: Edit Manipulation: Which Sentence Was Cut?
en.summary: Editing manipulation often removes one sentence; cut the premise and the conclusion changes.

en.title: Algorithm Feed: Why the Same Thing Again?
en.summary: Feeds amplify what holds attention; the longer you stay, the more it assumes you like it.

en.title: Clickbait: What the Title Promises, What the Body Gives
en.summary: Clickbait promises a strong result and delivers a weak example; summarize title and body separately.

en.title: Deepfake Detection: Look Beyond the Face
en.summary: Look beyond the face: teeth, ears, blinks, background text, and light direction.

en.title: Statistics Video: Did the Chart Lie?
en.summary: Check where the axis starts, what the total is, and whether the same group is compared.

en.title: Sponsorship Disclosure: Make the Ad Visible
en.summary: Disclose sponsorship before the recommendation, not in the last line of the description.

en.title: News Video: Scene, Secondhand Source, Verification
en.summary: Separate scene, secondhand source, and verification; an unverified scene is just footage.

en.title: Likeness, Location, and Minors: What a Release Must Say
en.summary: Consent to be filmed is not consent to be used commercially. Likeness, property, guardian consent for minors, and AI face/voice synthesis are four different clearances; a “consent to shoot” note will not save a paid ad.

en.title: Privacy and Blurring: When It Is Required
en.summary: Blurring is not politeness; addresses, plates, medical records, and minors need protection when identifiable.

en.title: Contract Scope: Price the “One More Revision” Before It Happens
en.summary: The most common film contract dispute is not payment; it is scope. Unclear deliverables, revisions, rights, acceptance, and termination become unpaid overtime.

en.title: Music Licensing: Sync, Performance, and Platform Libraries
en.summary: “I bought the song” does not mean “I can use it commercially.” Film projects must separate sync (recording into the film), performance (public playback), mechanical (copying audio), and master rights.

en.title: Location Release: What the Paper Says
en.summary: A location release states hours, areas, disruption, damage, and footage rights.

en.title: AI Content Labels: Explicit, Implicit, and Platform Duties
en.summary: AI content is not compliant with a single “AI” tag. China mainland rules distinguish explicit and implicit labels, with duties for platforms, tool providers, and publishers; ads and news are stricter.

en.title: Documentary Ethics: Filming Vulnerable People
en.summary: Ask three things: does he know the consequence, can he withdraw, and can the film hurt him.

en.title: Data Security: Client Privacy and Leaks
en.summary: Data security covers drives, cloud, chat, and forwarding; client privacy is not only the final cut.

en.title: Equipment and Production Insurance: What Is Covered, What Is Not
en.summary: Equipment insurance is not “broken, paid.” Separate property all-risks, machinery breakdown, public liability, and transit; deductibles, depreciation, exclusions, and claim documents decide payout.

en.title: Cross-border Production Invoices and Tax: Contract, Invoice, Withholding
en.summary: Cross-border projects stall on “invoices”: a proforma invoice is not a tax invoice. Place of service, receiving entity, permanent establishment, and withholding decide the tax. Confirm the path before quoting.

en.title: Image history: 1839, 1895, photography
en.summary: Image history is not a year list; 1839, 1895 and photography together show how recording became narrative.

en.title: Copyright chain: copyright, contract, music
en.summary: Copyright is not a line saying cleared; copyright, contract and music licence must match use, term and territory.

en.title: Media literacy: literacy, sources, algorithms
en.summary: Media literacy is not do not trust the internet; sources, algorithms and emotional triggers become checks.

en.title: AI compliance: labelling, deepfakes, data
en.summary: AI compliance is not one disclaimer; labelling, deepfakes and data provenance must pass together.

en.title: Platform History: From Channels to Feeds
en.summary: Platforms are not neutral containers. From channels to feeds, the entry, attention and duration changed, and so did the grammar of images.

en.title: Archive Ethics: Restoration, Alteration, Credit
en.summary: Archives are not neutral material. Restoration, alteration and credit all rewrite history; keep the original, the scope and the permission record.
